title: What If Every Cow Vanished Overnight?

scenes.text: What if every cow on Earth vanished overnight? The climate would feel it. So would a billion people.
There are around one and a half billion cattle, and they produce roughly nine percent of all human-caused greenhouse gases.
Most of that comes from methane, burped out as cows digest grass. Methane traps far more heat than carbon dioxide.
Emissions would fall, but livestock supply about a third of the world's protein.
Nearly a billion people depend on farm animals for their livelihoods, and many pastures cannot grow crops at all.
So the cow is both a climate problem and a lifeline. Removing it fixes one and breaks the other.
